name: Window-chrome screenshot settles under the word
looks: Under the headline word, a full product screenshot in a browser or app window frame slides and settles into frame, filling most of the lower half, with just enough real UI (a chart, a few labelled icon tiles) to read as a genuine screen rather than a mockup. The next card repeats the same move with a different screen (a video player instead of a dashboard), so the pair reads as two honest ways to show the same thing.
build: The window frame is a flat card with a thin top chrome bar (three dots, a URL-style strip); it tweens in from `y: 24px, opacity 0 -> y:0, opacity 1` on power2.out, 300-400ms, arriving just after the headline word. Internal UI elements (a line chart path draw-on, small icon tiles) settle 100-150ms after the frame itself lands, so the frame reads first and the content second.
sound: A soft whoosh under the window's slide, a light tick as the internal chart or tiles settle.
prompt: Under a headline word, slide a real product screen into frame inside a simple window chrome, filling most of the lower half, letting its own chart or UI elements settle in a beat after the frame arrives. Repeat the same move for a second, different kind of screen right after, so two cards together show the same capability two honest ways.
